fixes.explanation: Silver's a shiny guess, friend, but this verse says gold. Abijah, Judah's king, tells Israel they have with them “…the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.” Jeroboam is Israel's king. Gods that a man made himself! I can't even get my dough to listen to me, so I'm not about to ask it to run my life.

Joppa sounded good to me too, baker, but it never made this list. The text says Abijah, Judah's king, captured “Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, along with their villages.” He took them from Jeroboam, Israel's king. Bethel leads the list. I'd be a terrible mapmaker, though. I once got lost between my oven and my cooling rack.

Hebron sounds right, friend, and I get why you picked it. But the text says Abijah, Judah's king, captured “Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, along with their villages.” He took them from Jeroboam, Israel's king. Bethel is the first name on that list. Three cities AND their villages changed hands, and I still can't keep track of my own timer!
